name: Northfleet early Portland-cement kiln
description: At Northfleet, William Aspdin’s brick downdraught kiln produced early Portland cement from limestone and clay; later Portland cement routes differ.

date.label: Approximately 1846
date.basis: The cited source reports this approximate period or year; archaeological contexts date associated remains rather than a unique invention.

events.statement: Historic England dates construction of William Aspdin’s cement kiln to approximately 1846.

evidence.supports: Historic England dates construction of William Aspdin’s cement kiln to approximately 1846.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest sourced date for the specific documented case; this does not establish invention or worldwide priority.

caveats: The 1846 kiln date is approximate and does not establish first production on a specific day. The source connects Aspdin to higher-fired alite-bearing cement but does not prove every batch in this kiln had modern composition. Historic England describes William Aspdin as building the kiln to a patented design of Joseph Aspdin; the named-person contribution awaits a registered person.

research.note: Independently checked the circa 1846 construction and process attribution; kiln design is credited to Joseph Aspdin’s patent, not unambiguously William’s own design.
